subject: lang-dy
title: LANG.DY.------POL.DY.
description: Diagram in SR(TRS)II-40 (Social Reality / Trans-Information, Level Two), first of two on book p184. Accompanies Braxton's claim that 'the importance of defining terms cannot be overemphasized if we are to view social reality.' (C)LANG-DY (the concept of language dynamics) is crossed with POL-DY (political dynamics): the question is what language-dynamics produces when crossed with political-dynamics — language being the operational vehicle of definition, political-dynamics being the mechanism that determines whose definitions count. (R)TM (reality of time) feeds in from the upper-left. POL-DY sits at the upper-center. CU-AF-B (culture affinity basis) anchors the upper-right output. AF-COMP (affinity composite) and INT (interior) form the right output cluster. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) and IST-F-ALGN (interior-source-functionalism alignment) feed in from the upper-left. INFO-DS (information descent) and APP-RDEF (apparent redefinition) form the lower-right cluster. RE-DOC (redocumentation) and RE-ST (restructuralism) anchor the lower-left. Structural argument: language-dynamics-as-concept crossed with political-dynamics is mediated by multiple parallel upstreams (progressional-continuance, interior-source-functionalism-alignment, reality-of-time) — the unusual multi-upstream signature registers Braxton's structural commitment that definition is *over-determined* in a healthy system. The lower-output pair (information-descent and apparent-redefinition) is the diagnostic: when language-dynamics crosses with political-dynamics in the corrupted operative system, the output is information-descent into apparent-redefinition rather than into composite-affinity output. Redocumentation and restructuralism as lower upstreams are what must be live for the productive culture-affinity-basis output to obtain.
